Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning:
The user says they had some foods earlier. They want us to log them? Likely we should use the log_food function twice (or more). We have:

First part: "I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea." So that's 8 pieces of frozen mango; maybe also log the chai tea but it's not listed in allowed units? Allowed units include piece. For tea, no mention. But only logs for food items. Maybe skip beverage unless needed. Next: "Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee". That's 2 slices of pepperoni pizza. Coffee likely omitted.

We need to call log_food for each food item separately. Provide appropriate fields. Use default meal_type if unspecified. Probably breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack? Not known. Could assume snack. Also provide current timestamp? Or leave log_date null.

Thus produce calls:

{
"name": "frozen mango",
"portion_amount": 8,
"portion_unit":"piece"
}

and second:

{
"name":"pepperoni pizza slice",
"portion_amount":2,
"portion_unit":"slice"
}

But note naming: "pizza slice"? Might just say "pepperoni pizza".

Also might combine into one call per day? No separate calls.
